name: intraday_range_reversion_v154
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: NIFTY's intraday session high and low act as psychological ceilings and floors where order flow clusters. When NIFTY touches its running session high, limit sell orders from institutions who scaled in during the move defend that level, and retail breakout buyers who just entered become the fuel for a reversion when the level holds. At 5-second resolution, we detect rejection at the session extreme by measuring the wick ratio of the bar that touches the extreme: if the upper wick exceeds 70% of the bar's total range while price is within 2 spot points of the session high, market makers who sold at that high are actively defending their position. The rejection bar is the fingerprint of supply overwhelming demand at a known level. On NIFTY, the reversion from a defended session extreme typically covers 10-20 spot points (5-10 ATM option points) over 1-3 minutes as breakout buyers unwind and mean-reversion algos activate. This strategy is fundamentally different from PDH/PDL fakeout (which trades PREVIOUS day's levels that have overnight significance), different from VWAP reversion (which trades deviation from volume-weighted average price, not from session extremes), and different from z-score reversion (which uses statistical deviation from rolling mean). Here, the key level is TODAY's running high/low — a dynamic level that only exists because of the session's own price discovery process. We buy ATM PE when NIFTY rejects the session high, and ATM CE when NIFTY bounces off the session low.

indicators.name: session_high
indicators.purpose: Tracks the highest price NIFTY has reached today. This level is watched by every participant — breakout traders set buy-stops above it, institutions who sold near it defend it, and algos reference it for range calculations. The session-level lookback is essential because unlike a fixed-period rolling high, the session high only moves UP (never down), making it a progressively stronger level as more traders anchor to it throughout the day.

indicators.name: session_low
indicators.purpose: Tracks the lowest price NIFTY has reached today. Mirror of session_high for the downside — breakout sellers set sell-stops below it, institutions who bought near it defend it. Session-level lookback ensures this is today's true floor, not a rolling window artifact.

indicators.name: distance_to_high
indicators.purpose: Measures how close the current bar's high is to the session high. A value of 0 means the bar touched or exceeded the session high. We require distance_to_high <= 2 spot points to trigger the pattern, because on NIFTY at 5-second resolution, the session high test often comes within 1-2 points rather than hitting it exactly — market makers front-run the level by pulling bids 1-2 points early.

indicators.name: distance_to_low
indicators.purpose: Measures how close the current bar's low is to the session low. A value of 0 means the bar touched or exceeded the session low. Same 2-point proximity logic as distance_to_high.

indicators.name: upper_wick_ratio
indicators.purpose: Measures what fraction of the bar's range is upper wick (rejection from above). A ratio > 0.70 on a bar touching the session high means 70%+ of the bar's movement was rejected — price spiked up to the extreme and was immediately pushed back down within that 5-second window. This is the micro-signature of active selling defense. The 0.01 epsilon prevents division by zero on doji bars. On NIFTY, wick ratios above 0.70 at session extremes precede 10+ point reversions about 55% of the time.

indicators.name: lower_wick_ratio
indicators.purpose: Measures what fraction of the bar's range is lower wick (rejection from below). A ratio > 0.70 on a bar touching the session low means the bar probed the low and bounced back — the micro-signature of buying defense at the session floor.

indicators.name: session_range
indicators.purpose: The total NIFTY range established so far today. We require session_range > 30 spot points to ensure the session high/low are meaningful levels with genuine order clustering, not just the narrow band of the first 15 minutes. On NIFTY, the average daily range is 100-200 spot points; a 30-point minimum ensures the extremes have been tested by real directional flow.

indicators.name: bars_since_extreme_set
indicators.formula: bars since session_high or session_low was last updated
indicators.purpose: Counts how many 5-second bars have elapsed since the current session extreme was established. We require at least 60 bars (5 minutes) since the extreme was set — this ensures the session high/low has 'aged' enough for resting orders to accumulate around it. A brand-new session high that was just set 10 seconds ago has no accumulated order defense yet. On NIFTY, it takes 3-5 minutes of stable extreme for limit orders and stop-losses to cluster around the level.

conditions: distance_to_low <= 2 (NIFTY bar touches or comes within 2 spot points of session low — testing the floor)
lower_wick_ratio > 0.70 (70%+ of the bar is lower wick — strong rejection/bounce from the session low level)
session_range > 30 (session range is wide enough that the low is a meaningful level with order clustering)
bars_since_extreme_set > 60 (session low was established at least 5 minutes ago — sufficient time for resting orders to accumulate around it)
buy_ce.confirmation: The rejection bar must close above its midpoint (close > (high + low) / 2) AND the bar's range must be at least 3 spot points (not a tiny doji). This confirms genuine buying pressure at the session low, not just a low-volume tick fluctuation.

conditions: distance_to_high <= 2 (NIFTY bar touches or comes within 2 spot points of session high — testing the ceiling)
upper_wick_ratio > 0.70 (70%+ of the bar is upper wick — strong rejection from the session high level)
session_range > 30 (session range is wide enough that the high is a meaningful level)
bars_since_extreme_set > 60 (session high was established at least 5 minutes ago)
buy_pe.confirmation: The rejection bar must close below its midpoint (close < (high + low) / 2) AND the bar's range must be at least 3 spot points. This confirms genuine selling pressure at the session high.

exit.stop_rationale: A 5-option-point stop corresponds to roughly 10 spot points beyond the session extreme. If NIFTY breaks through the session high/low by 10+ spot points, the extreme has genuinely broken — this is no longer a rejection, it is a breakout. On NIFTY, false rejections that turn into breakouts typically move 8-15 spot points through the old extreme within 30-60 seconds. The 5-point option stop (~10 spot points) catches the break before the full breakout develops, limiting loss to approximately one 30-second adverse move (2-5 option points typical).
exit.target_rationale: After a confirmed rejection of the session extreme, NIFTY typically reverts 10-20 spot points (5-10 option points) toward the session midpoint over 1-3 minutes. The 8-point target captures the majority of this reversion (roughly 60-80% of the typical move) without requiring price to reach the full session midpoint, which only happens about 30% of the time. This provides a 1.6:1 reward-to-risk ratio against the 5-point stop — sufficient edge when the win rate is ~50% because rejected session extremes have a natural base rate above random.

filters.vix_filter: VIX between 12-25 — below 12, NIFTY's session range is too narrow (often < 30 points) for meaningful session extreme reversion; above 25, session extremes are frequently broken by volatile momentum and the rejection pattern has a much lower success rate
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:45 (need 30 minutes for session extremes to establish with genuine order clustering) or after 14:30 — late-session extreme tests are distorted by closing flows and gamma hedging
filters.volume_filter: The rejection bar should have volume > 1.2x the 60-bar SMA — elevated volume on the rejection confirms active participation at the extreme, not just a low-liquidity price drift to the level
filters.trend_filter: Stronger edge when the rejection aligns with the broader session trend: rejecting the session high in a day that is trading below VWAP (sellers in control, high is natural resistance) has higher win rate than rejecting the high in a strong uptrend day
filters.spread_filter: Skip if ATM option bid-ask > 2.5 points — at session extremes, option market makers may widen spreads in anticipation of a breakout, increasing the cost of entry

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — session extreme rejection is a structural phenomenon driven by resting order clustering and market maker defense, not a widely automated signal at 5-second resolution

adaptation_notes: Four major changes from the original 1-minute stock-level intraday range reversion to 5-second NIFTY index options: (1) Universe shifted from NIFTY 200 stocks to NIFTY index itself. Stock-level session highs/lows have idiosyncratic noise (block deals, corporate actions); NIFTY index session extremes are pure market-wide sentiment levels with broader order clustering. (2) The pin bar / hammer detection was refined for 5-second resolution. On 1-minute bars, a pin bar represents 60 seconds of rejection; on 5-second bars, we need a MORE EXTREME wick ratio (>70% vs the original's >70%) because a single 5-second bar shows the immediate micro-rejection but has less statistical weight. We compensate by requiring the session extreme to have 'aged' 5+ minutes (bars_since_extreme_set > 60), ensuring the level has accumulated order defense. (3) Target changed from '50% of intraday range toward midpoint' (which on NIFTY could be 50-100 spot points, requiring a 15-30 minute hold) to a fixed 8 option points that captures the initial reversion impulse of 1-3 minutes. The original acknowledged this target was 'ambitious' — our shorter, more realistic target trades the reliable initial reversion rather than hoping for full mean reversion. (4) The original required 60 bars (1 hour) for the range to establish; we require 60 bars (5 minutes) since the specific extreme was set, which is a different and more precise filter — it measures order accumulation at the level rather than general range establishment.
weaknesses: On genuine breakout days where NIFTY trends strongly in one direction, the first test of the session extreme IS the beginning of the next impulse leg — the wick rejection is a momentary pause, not a true reversal, and the strategy catches the wrong side

Near NIFTY round numbers (22000, 22500, etc.) that coincide with session extremes, the order clustering is more complex due to options gamma hedging, and the rejection pattern can be overwhelmed by hedging flows

The 5-minute aging requirement (bars_since_extreme_set > 60) means missing the very first rejection of a newly established extreme, which can sometimes be the strongest reversion signal when the extreme was set by a news-driven spike

On weekly expiry days (Thursdays), session extremes near popular strike prices attract gamma-driven flows that create artificial rejections — the wick looks like defense but is actually delta hedging, and the reversion may not follow through
The strategy generates no signals on narrow-range days (session range < 30 points) which occur 15-20% of trading days, leaving the capital idle
